thread:
alice_support: FYI customer acme-corp reported sudden p95/p99 spike ~10:12 UTC. They also saw repeated OOMs on one GPU pool and a bunch of slab evictions. Ticket SUP-4821. Logs attached in ticket.
deploy-bot: Alert: GPU-MEM-PRESSURE pool-gpu-east-3 host=gpu-03 alert=oom_count>3 in 15m
bob_runtime: Can you paste the minimal repro (request body + model + tenant id)? Any recent rollout to that pool?
alice_support: tenant=acme-42
alice_support: sample curl (from customer):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-qa","prompt":"long conversation...","max_tokens":2048,"stream":false}'
```
alice_support: They say latency p95 jumped from ~300ms to 1.8s and p99 to ~5s. GPU oom logs:
```
[2026-03-16T09:57:12Z] GPU_OOM: slab_alloc failed alloc_bytes=134217728 kv_items=1.2e6 free_frag=0.08
[2026-03-16T09:57:13Z] evict: slab_evicted=128 entries=4096 reason=kv_pressure
[2026-03-16T09:57:16Z] slow-path p99=5.2s queue_depth=24
```
bob_runtime: Interesting — kv_items 1.2M indicates KV growth. Do we have per-tenant KV size histograms? Can SLO routing be triggered?
dave_oncall: Quick mitigation options:
- route acme-42 to smaller variant (gptx-8b) or to dedicated cold pool
- set tenant-level max_tokens=512 / disable streaming heavy context
- force kv-evict for tenant or restart worker to defragment slabs
carla_sre: Commands to inspect host:
```
ssh gpu-03
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
redwoodctl mem inspect --host gpu-03 --slabs
# slab summary: redwoodctl mem inspect shows slab_density=0.93, free_frag_pct=7
rbtop --proc slab_compaction
```
carla_sre: Also check allocator counters in /proc/redwood/alloc_stats (showed high alloc churn: alloc_retries=1223, compactions=2)
erin_engineer: Short-term patch: enable per-tenant kv-ttl (30m) and aggressive kv-evict for this tenant. Steps I can run if oncall approves:
1) redwoodctl tenant update acme-42 --kv-ttl=1800 --kv-evict=true
2) rollout small-model routing: redwoodctl route set --tenant acme-42 --model gptx-8b --percent 100
3) on hosts with high frag: systemctl restart redwood-worker@pool-gpu-east-3 (drains first)
dave_oncall: Approve. Do step 1+2 now. I'll schedule a rolling restart for gpu-03 after routing finishes (to avoid customer downtime).
alice_support: Customer ok with temporary perf drop; they asked for repro steps we can use internally.
bob_runtime: Repro checklist for eng-runtime:
- run a load script that mimics long chats and many unique prefixes to force KV growth
- set sequence length=2048, concurrency=30, max_tokens=2048
- monitor /metrics for redwood_kv_items, slab_free_frag_pct, redwood_alloc_retries
erin_engineer: Here's a quick load command we used in staging:
```
python tools/loadgen.py --model gptx-13b-qa --concurrency 30 --seq 2048 --unique-prefixes 100000 --duration 30m --tenant acme-42
```
carla_sre: Longer-term: tuning ideas
- increase slab compaction frequency (compact_interval from 600s -> 120s)
- bump allocator reserve pool to 1GB on affected machine types
- add proactive KV eviction thresholds per-tenant
- consider transparent model-quantization fallback for tail traffic
bob_runtime: I'll prep a runtime PR with knobs: --slab-compact-interval, --allocator-reserve, and per-tenant kv-ttl defaults. Will include metrics to track compaction latency.
alice_support: Thanks team — I updated SUP-4821 with mitigation steps and timelines. I'll notify customer once routing and TTL change are applied. :thumbsup:
